claims.text: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has excellent mechanical strength at 1600 °C.
Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has very poor room-temperature ductility.
The irradiation resistance of NbMoTaW is excellent.
Substituting approximately 5 at.% of the base alloy with vanadium can retain a single-phase BCC structure.
Using identical melting, casting, and homogenization conditions guarantees comparable grain sizes and phase homogeneity between the baseline and modified alloys.
Vanadium addition induces local lattice softening in NbMoTaW.
Vanadium-induced local lattice softening reduces the Peierls barrier for dislocation motion at room temperature.
Vanadium has a lower modulus than the refractory elements in the NbMoTaW matrix.
Vanadium has a lower melting point than the refractory elements in the NbMoTaW matrix.
Vanadium alters the local bonding environment and electronic structure of NbMoTaW.
A reduced energy barrier for dislocation glide enhances room-temperature ductility.
Approximately 5 at.% vanadium does not alter the overall BCC phase stability.
Retention of the BCC phase ensures retention of high-temperature strength and irradiation resistance.
The vanadium-modified alloy will have greater room-temperature strain-to-failure than untreated NbMoTaW.
The vanadium-modified alloy will retain 1600 °C mechanical performance comparable to untreated NbMoTaW.
The vanadium-modified alloy will retain irradiation resistance comparable to untreated NbMoTaW.
The intervention is effective only when the vanadium concentration is kept near 5 at.%.
Excess vanadium may produce additional phases or compromise high-temperature performance.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field describes irradiation resistance as an established excellent property, whereas the baseline field describes it as predicted. These are inconsistent epistemic characterizations.

A quinary alloy containing only about 5 at.% V is not equiatomic across all five elements, despite the intervention describing the resulting overall composition as near equiatomic. The intended redistribution among Nb, Mo, Ta, and W is not explicitly defined.
